title: Stability Sentinel: automated regression detection and controlled republish for verified model profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Verified performance profiles (latency/throughput/cost) published to the catalog can silently regress over time due to model updates, infra drift, or different workload distributions. Current republish flows are manual and slow, and we lack an automated detection + safe republish/rollback mechanism that ties telemetry, sampled canaries, and human signoff into a repeatable flow.

Goal: Deliver a ‘Stability Sentinel’ orchestration that continuously evaluates profile health, automatically opens a gated republish workflow when regressions are detected, and provides deterministic rollback actions when canary or rollout metrics breach safety guards. The system should reduce time-to-remediation, keep customers pinned to stable profiles, and create auditable artifacts (logs, PRs, approvals) for changes to verified profiles.
acceptance_criteria: Stability Sentinel runs hourly over production telemetry and flags profiles with statistically significant latency or throughput regressions relative to pinned signatures

When a regression is flagged, the system triggers an isolated canary run against a sampled traffic slice and produces a candidate republish PR with performance artifacts and a clear rollback recommendation

Canary gating evaluates cost-normalized metrics, token-distribution coverage, and output-quality regression signals; if canary passes, UI exposes a one-click promote with audit log and time-delayed auto-promote option
If canary fails or downstream consumer errors spike, the system auto-creates a rollback workflow and pins affected customers to last-known-good profile until human remediation
All actions (detect, PR, promote, rollback) are logged to the audit ledger and surfaced in console notifications and Slack channel #profile-ops with links to artifacts
End-to-end smoke tests and a staged experiment confirm <1% false-positive rate on synthetic no-regression workloads and >80% detection rate on injected regressions in our test harness
tasks: Define statistical regression thresholds and sampling heuristics (PM + Applied ML)
Extend telemetry contract to emit per-profile sliding-window histograms and token distribution fingerprints
Build an evaluation runner that can execute isolated canary workload using shadow traffic; integrate with existing benchmark harness
Create automated PR generator that composes performance artifacts, difference visualizations, and recommended pin/rollback actions
Add console UI: sentinel dashboard, per-profile status, one-click promote/rollback, and optional auto-promote timer
Add RBAC and approval gates for enterprise-managed profiles; include audit logs and signed attestations
Wire Slack/Email alerts and a runbook link for on-call follow-up
Security review and KMS/HSM check for any signing actions on profile artifacts
Write integration tests, chaos tests (simulate infra regressions), and canary failure scenarios
Ship behind feature flag and run a 6-week pilot on 10% of traffic for low-risk profiles
notes: This ticket focuses on orchestration and safety guards. Metric definitions and exact thresholds will be iterated with Applied ML and Runtime teams in the first two weeks. We will avoid auto-unpinning customer-facing profiles without explicit enterprise opt-in. The feature flag must default to off for all enterprise tenants until SSO+RBAC flows are validated.
risks: False positives causing unnecessary republish churn
Automatic promotion could surface regression if canary sampling is unrepresentative
Audit/signing gaps could break compliance requirements for enterprise customers
Cost of frequent canaries if sampling rate is too high
mitigations: Conservative initial thresholds and require human approval by default
Run canaries on shadow traffic and use stratified sampling across token-length buckets
Require security review + signed attestations for any automated promote path
Cost caps and quota enforcement for canary runner; throttle retry/backoff
